### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eb20c33c456f4b9fdeafd0e7a5b5de274888848e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cf5f72c416cef64a4a1ea4256c251fcd0ec8840b` — the merge of head `9eb65e6a449c2135a7968283e961c5157de51fa5` into base `eb20c33c456f4b9fdeafd0e7a5b5de274888848e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cf5f72c416cef64a4a1ea4256c251fcd0ec8840b && git checkout cf5f72c416cef64a4a1ea4256c251fcd0ec8840b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin eb20c33c456f4b9fdeafd0e7a5b5de274888848e 9eb65e6a449c2135a7968283e961c5157de51fa5 && git checkout -B drift-repro eb20c33c456f4b9fdeafd0e7a5b5de274888848e && git merge --no-ff 9eb65e6a449c2135a7968283e961c5157de51fa5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eb20c33c456f4b9fdeafd0e7a5b5de274888848e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

**DELIBERATE CORRECTION — `Check Changeset` is red by design on this PR.** `domain:engine` seat 2 · `session_01ADzJtzYTLUfgrRZHxkagkX` · 2026-10-11T23:57Z.

- **The gate:** `check-empty-changeset.mjs`'s foreign-changeset refusal in the `Check Changeset` job of `pr-automation.yml`. Its one error line names `.changeset/22782-objectql-after-hook-abort-rolls-back.md`; the job's other steps pass.
- **Why it is red:** commit `4a3e842580` rewrites one clause of that pending note's "Unchanged" bullet, a note this PR did not add. It said "No unit is opened for an `onError: 'log'` hook, an `async: true` hook, …". This PR makes the door open a unit for such a hook when it carries a `condition`, so the clause now reads "an `onError: 'log'` or `async: true` hook that carries no `condition` (#22856)". Restoring it would ship a false sentence in the next CHANGELOG. Commit `48b64091df` drops this PR's own note's pointer to that line, since the line now says it itself.
- **Why it may land red:** the gate's own source names this class red by design; `Check Changeset` runs on `pull_request` only, not on `merge_group`, and is not a required context. A same-head contract-tier record confirms the corrected sentence before this seat arms the queue.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `48b64091df805f10264f295c69f21b01eda61e4c`
Local-runs: none

Read-only shape held: the card #22856 (body and all five comments: triage 6110316957, claim 6114412794, os-dev-report 6115299755, file-surface addendum 6115328926, os-dev-report 6115564493), PR #22906 (body, both comments, file list, commit list), the 42 check-runs on the head, the net diff of the branch against `origin/main` (merge-base `3f694715ee`, 7 files, +269/-59, identical to the PR's file list), and the `origin/main` readings the brief allows (`packages/objectql/package.json`, `src/index.ts`, `src/hook-wrappers.ts`, `src/engine.ts` around `opensAfterAbortUnit` and its three call sites, `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`, `content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx`). Two reads beyond that list, named here because they decided a finding: the gate's own statement of what the `Clause-②` line asks (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`), and, following PR #22819's round-4 remediation which the family card cites, the two sibling pages that restate the door's rule (`content/docs/api/data-flow.mdx`, `content/docs/kernel/events.mdx`). Nothing was built, run or re-run; the git fetch of the branch into a review ref is a read of objects.

**Check-runs at the final read:** 42, all completed, none pending. 36 success (Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core 1/6 to 6/6 and the aggregate, Dogfood Regression Gate 1/3 to 3/3 and the aggregate, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Lint and Repo Gates, the four Type Check lanes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, the four PR-claim guards, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected), 4 skipped (Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke opt-in, and Auto Label plus Check PR Size on the second `pull_request` run), 2 failure: **`Check Changeset`, twice** (the first run and the re-run after the body edit). Each red carries exactly one failing annotation, naming `.changeset/22782-objectql-after-hook-abort-rolls-back.md` as present on the merge base and changed by this PR, with the gate's two-class text (COLLISION / DELIBERATE CORRECTION). No other check is red. The PR is a same-repo branch (not a fork), draft, auto-merge not armed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Which writes now open the door's unit — RIGHT.** `opensAfterAbortUnit` (engine.ts) keeps its first line (an open threaded or ambient unit: no unit of its own; the closed-handle reading from PR #22894 kept), its `skipAutomations` exit, and its tail (default driver only, and only one that declares transactions). The only changed expression is the `aborting` test: a metadata-bound entry (`entry.meta`, so a code-registered `registerHook` entry still never counts) matching the object, that EITHER is blocking with `onError` `abort`/omitted (the #22782 arm, unchanged) OR has `declaredHookCondition(entry.meta)` defined. So an `after*` hook carrying a condition opens the unit whatever its `onError` and `async`, on `afterInsert`, `afterUpdate` and `afterDelete` only (the three call sites are untouched; a `before*` hook never reaches the predicate, and its abort refuses before anything is stored).
- **Which still do not — RIGHT, each one.** No condition on a `log` or `async` hook (the second disjunct is undefined, the first fails on `log` or on `async`); `skipAutomations` (exit unchanged; pinned by the unit CONTROL, zero begins); off the default datasource and a driver with no transactions (tail unchanged); a write already inside a unit (first line unchanged); a hook registered in code (no `meta`). An `abort` plus `async: true` hook with a condition is newly counted, correctly: the gate can abort it before it detaches.
- **"Carries a condition" has one reading — RIGHT, by construction.** `declaredHookCondition(meta)` returns the Expression envelope (string shorthand lifted to `cel`) only when its `source` is non-blank, else undefined. `wrapDeclarativeHook` now installs its `conditionFn` on exactly `if (expr)` over that value, and the compile/evaluate block inside is the pre-change code one nesting level shallower (same compile, same `unevaluableConditionError` and `uncompilableConditionError` throws, same compile-failure log line). The door tests the same function for `!== undefined`. So the ast-only envelope the dev notes (no `source`) installs no gate and opens no unit, as before, and the door cannot disagree with the gate on any shape. The wrapper's step order is unchanged: the gate runs first, synchronously, outside `runWithErrorPolicy` and before the `fireAndForget` branch, which is why a `log` or `async` hook's unevaluable condition aborts the write — the premise the whole change rests on.
- **Not on the published surface — RIGHT.** `declaredHookCondition` is a module export of `hook-wrappers.ts`; neither `src/index.ts` (the `.` entry: `wrapDeclarativeHook`, `HookConditionError`, `hookRecordState`, the `WrapDeclarativeOptions` type) nor `src/core.ts` (the `./core` entry) re-exports it and neither file is in the diff; `package.json` `exports` maps only `.` and `./core`, so no deep import reaches it. Per the contract-review reference, a symbol unreachable from the entry type graph and not addressable through `exports` is shipped bytes, not published accept set. `engine.ts` gains a value import from `hook-wrappers.ts`; `hook-wrappers.ts` imports only a type from `engine.ts`, so no runtime cycle (Build Core and the dual-build gate are green).
- **A condition that EVALUATES behaves as before — RIGHT as pinned, with one gap carried to ②.** `false` still skips (gate unchanged; pinned by the second insert in the `log` CONTROL). `true` with `onError: 'log'` and a throwing handler: `[hook] handler failed (onError=log; suppressing)` logged, both rows stored, zero rollbacks (unit CONTROL) and REST `201` with the row stored (dogfood CONTROL). An `async: true` hook with a true condition now starts inside the door's unit and its 40 ms late `ctx.api` write still lands (dogfood CONTROL, exercising the #22855 closed-handle path on the new population). Test Core and the three Dogfood lanes are green on this head. The gap: "as before" is not exact for a hook body whose `ctx.api` write runs inside the new unit, see ②.
- **Docs table row (`hooks.mdx`, the unit-of-work table) — RIGHT.** The first row now names "a blocking one whose `onError` is `abort` (the default), or one carrying a `condition`, whatever its `onError` and `async`", with the second cell's two exclusions kept. It matches the predicate. Kept imprecision, not introduced: the row says "an `after*` hook" where the predicate requires a metadata-bound one, as the previous wording did. Sibling restatements left as they were: ③.
- **Cost line — RIGHT.** The unit is opened per write on every object carrying such a hook, not only on writes whose condition fails (the door cannot know in advance), so "one transaction per write on objects that carry such a hook" is the true cost, the same as #22782's. The in-repo reach (the two showcase `async: true, onError: 'log'` `afterUpdate` hooks on `showcase_task` and `showcase_project`) is the dev's measurement, reported here as such and not re-measured.
- **Pins — adequate.** Unit: `log` insert (refused with `HookConditionError`, `reason: 'unevaluable'`, hook and event named; row and the `log` chain-writer's note absent; one begin, one rollback), `log` on update and delete (stored row unchanged, two begins, two rollbacks), `async` (refused, row absent, handler never ran), plus the three CONTROLs. The dev's first-draft confound (an `abort` chain writer that opened the unit by itself) was caught and replaced, which is the right fix. Real door: five REST `createData` cases on the verify stack, including the `async` late-write CONTROL. Ablation evidence is the dev's; CI's green on the head is what this record relies on.

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: no` — RIGHT as the gate defines the axis.** PR body line 2 reads `Clause-②: no`; the changeset `.changeset/22856-log-hook-unevaluable-condition.md` declares `Clause-②: no`; the card's triage grade (6110316957) and claim (6114412794) both say `no`. The gate's own text asks whether the PR puts a new key on a published payload, widens an accept set or enlarges the public surface. This diff adds no authorable key, no payload key, no `exports`-reachable symbol, and refuses nothing an author could write before. `patch` for `@objectstack/objectql` is the level the repo assigns a bug fix in a released package. `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-adr-0087-registration` are inside the green Lint and Repo Gates.
- **Escalated, not a FAIL ground: the family precedent read the same mechanism the other way.** PR #22819 (#22782, merged two days before this head) declared `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and shipped `minor` with an ADR-0087 marker, explicitly for what happens INSIDE the door's unit: a hook body's cross-datasource `ctx.api` business write is refused with `CrossDatasourceTransactionWriteError` under the #5696 rule, and a MongoDB default store needs a replica set for the unit; its seat ruled (Q1, Q2) that the changeset must name that population and the remedy. This PR extends the identical unit to a new population (every write on an object carrying a `log` or `async` hook with a condition) and inherits those consequences unchanged, under `no`/`patch`. The owning seat decides on the next head whether this stays `no`/`patch` (defensible under the gate's definition, and this record's reading) or matches the family's `yes (narrowing)`/`minor` with the marker; the record does not refuse the PR on the arm alone.
- **The changeset TEXT, however, does not match what the diff publishes — FAIL ground F2.** The 22856 note's "Unchanged" paragraph opens "a condition that evaluates behaves as before". On this head a condition that evaluates TRUE now runs its hook inside the door's unit, so, by the family note's own statement about this unit: a blocking `onError: 'log'` hook whose body writes a business row to an object on another datasource has that write refused and logged where it used to land (the caller still gets its row); the same holds for the part of an `async: true` body that runs before the unit's callback settles; and a MongoDB default store without a replica set now refuses writes to objects carrying such a hook, where it accepted them. The note names neither population nor a remedy (drop the `condition`, or `async: true` for a late cross-datasource write, or one datasource / a replica set). That is the sentence #22782's seat ruled a changeset in this family must carry. One sentence fixes it. Everything else in the note is true on this head (the FROM/TO paragraphs, `false` skips, `true` plus `log` logs and stores, `async` late writes land, inside-a-unit joins, the three non-opening exits, `log`/`async` with no condition opens no unit, the cost line).

### ③ Boundary flags

**The DELIBERATE CORRECTION (PR comment 6115345828, the seat's note; addendum 6115328926 on the card).** Named and judged:

- **Commit `4a3e842580`** touches only `.changeset/22782-objectql-after-hook-abort-rolls-back.md`, one line, blob `f02b523a08` to `2364fe4a54`. The blob at the merge-base equals the blob on current `origin/main` (`eb20c33c45`, after `main` moved past `9963322fe8`), so no third party's edit to that note is overwritten. Word-diff: two token runs only ("hook, an" to "or"; "hook," to "hook that carries no `condition` (#22856),"). Front matter (`minor`), title, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, the ADR-0087 marker, the BREAKING paragraph, FROM, TO, the three later bullets and the cost bullet are byte-identical. **Nothing else in the file changed: confirmed.**
- **The rewritten sentence, clause by clause, on this head:** (a) "No unit is opened for an `onError: 'log'` or `async: true` hook that carries no `condition`" — TRUE (second disjunct undefined, first fails on `log` or `async`), and its converse, that such a hook WITH a condition opens one, is this PR; (b) "a hook registered in code with `registerHook` (no declared `onError`)" — TRUE, the `entry.meta` guard is kept; (c) "a write with `skipAutomations`" — TRUE, exit kept; (d) "an object whose datasource is not the default one" — TRUE, tail kept; (e) "a default driver with no transactions (ADR-0119 D1, ...)" — TRUE, tail kept; (f) "On those the row stays stored after an abort, as before" — TRUE for every population the sentence now lists. **The rewritten clause is true.**
- **But the file is not yet wholly true on this head — FAIL ground F1.** Two bullets below, the "Inside the new unit, the rules of any unit apply" bullet still ends "If either applies to you, mark the hook `onError: 'log'` or `async: true`, or keep the objects on one datasource." After this PR, marking a hook that carries a `condition` as `log` or `async` no longer takes its object out of the unit; the cross-datasource refusal and the replica-set requirement stay. The correction's own reason ("restoring it would ship a false sentence") applies to that remedy word for word, and it is the prescription an upgrading reader greps. One clause fixes it (the remedy holds for a hook with no `condition`; otherwise drop the condition, or one datasource). Until then this record cannot confirm that the deliberately changed note is true, which is what the seat said a same-head record must do before arming.
- **Commit `48b64091df`** removes the last sentence of the 22856 note's "Unchanged" paragraph (the pointer at the 22782 line's old wording). After `4a3e842580` that sentence described text that no longer exists, so removing it leaves the note **no less true**: every remaining sentence holds except the "behaves as before" opener (F2), which predates round 1.
- The seat's note also says the gate's class is red by design, runs on `pull_request` only and is not a required context; this record relied on the check-run conclusions alone and did not read the workflow, so that part is the seat's statement, not verified here.

**Dev flags, round 0 (report 6115299755).** Deviations: (1) `hooks.mdx` row beyond the claim's surface — accepted, declared cross-lane in the addendum; the row is right (①). (2) Ablation restore preflight in present mode — a process note on a DELETE ablation; not re-run; CI green on the head is the evidence used. (3) `origin/main` merged with a merge commit — the net diff against the merge-base is the seven files above; fine. (4) First union stopped and re-run on `9ba561108f` — superseded by round 1's union and by CI on this head. (5) A stray whole-repo eslint, output discarded — no evidence cited from it; Lint and Repo Gates green. (6) Narrowed dogfood `tsc` — the four Type Check lanes are green on the head. (7) Attribution: commits carry `Claude-Session` plus a model-free `Co-authored-by`, the PR footer carries the session link — matches the commit list read here; AGENTS.md's rule wins, accepted. Out-of-scope findings: (1) load-time refusal of a never-bindable condition — population measured 0, not filed per triage, accepted. (2) The 22782 note's "Unchanged" clause — became the DELIBERATE CORRECTION; judged above, with F1 on the same file. (3) ast-only envelope installs no gate — pre-existing, and the shared reading makes the door agree with the gate on it; accepted. Open questions: none.

**Dev flags, round 1 (report 6115564493).** Deviations: (1) `origin/main` moved and was not merged — CI tested the merge of this head into the then `main`; the 22782 blob is identical on current `main`; accepted. (2) Rebuild from the turbo cache before the union — accepted. (3) Push-count correction — noted. Out-of-scope findings: none. Open questions: none. The report's `pr_body_sentences_this_round_makes_false` replacements are all present in the PR body as read; one nit for the seat's next body edit: the "Acceptance notes" bullet says "See Deliberate correction below" while that section sits above it.

**Escalated to the owning seat (not FAIL grounds).** (E1) The Clause-② arm against the family precedent, ② above. (E2) Three untouched restatements of the door's rule that this PR widens: `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`, the `HookEvent` JSDoc's "Four ordinary ways a write ends up inside such a unit", first bullet (blocking `abort` only), and the `onError` TSDoc's "the unit the write door opens for a blocking `abort` `after*` hook"; `content/docs/api/data-flow.mdx`, the `afterInsert/Update/Delete` row; `content/docs/kernel/events.mdx`, the `onError: 'abort'` bullet. The two doc lines stay true about their subject (what `abort` does) and link to the corrected `hooks.mdx` section; the spec JSDoc enumeration is under-inclusive the same way the `hooks.mdx` row was before this PR fixed it. Touching `packages/spec` enlarges the surface (PR #22819 did it with a spec `patch` changeset and a regenerated reference page), so this is the seat's call: fold in on the next head, or file it. The generated `content/docs/references/data/hook.mdx` row and the `onError` `describe()` string are unqualified ("for an after* hook on an object on the default datasource") and stay true. (E3) The sanitised `500` and triage's third option stay out, as triage ruled.

**What a PASS on the next head needs:** F1 (one clause in the 22782 note's remedy) and F2 (one sentence in the 22856 note naming the inside-the-unit consequences for this population and the remedy), the seat's decision on E1 reflected in both the PR body line 2 and the changeset, and a new same-head record. No source, test or doc-table change is owed by this review.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9eb65e6a449c2135a7968283e961c5157de51fa5`
Local-runs: none

Read-only shape held. Inputs: card #22856 (body and all seven comments: triage 6110316957, claim 6114412794, os-dev-reports 6115299755, 6115564493 and 6116082195, file-surface addendum 6115328926, the seat's ruling 6115782204), PR #22906 (title, body, its three comments including the DELIBERATE CORRECTION note 6115345828 and the earlier record 6115773915, the seven-file list), the 42 check-runs on the head with the two `Check Changeset` jobs' step lists and annotations, and the net diff of the branch against `origin/main` (fetched into a review ref of this session's own; merge-base `3f694715ee`; 7 files, +278/-60, identical to the PR's file list). `origin/main` readings the brief allows: `packages/objectql/package.json`, `src/index.ts`, `src/core.ts`, `src/hook-wrappers.ts`, `src/engine.ts` around `opensAfterAbortUnit`, its three call sites, `HookEntry` and `enforceTransactionOrigin`, `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`, `content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx`, and the three changeset gates' own text (`check-empty-changeset.mjs`, `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` with the `Clause-②` reader it imports, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`). Two reads beyond that list, named because they decided a sentence below: AGENTS.md's required-context list (Multi-agent discipline §7), and one grep of the hand-written `content/docs` tree at the head for `onError: 'log'` / `async: true` restatements. Nothing was built, run or re-run; the record template was printed as the brief prescribes.

**Since the earlier head `48b64091df`:** `git diff 48b64091df..head --stat` names exactly two files, `.changeset/22782-objectql-after-hook-abort-rolls-back.md` (+1/-1) and `.changeset/22856-log-hook-unevaluable-condition.md` (+15/-7). The source, test and docs-table hunks are byte-identical to the ones record 6115773915 judged; they are re-judged below all the same. `origin/main` (now `7dbb89dc5d`) has not moved on any of the seven files since the merge-base, and the 22782 note's blob on current `main` equals the merge-base blob, so no third party's edit is overwritten.

**Check-runs at the final read:** 42, all completed, none pending. 36 success, among them every one of the seven required contexts (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` with its six shards, `Dogfood Regression Gate` with its three, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`), plus Build Docs, Dogfood Verify CLI, the four Type Check lanes, Spec property liveness, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected, and the four PR-claim guards on both `pull_request` runs. 4 skipped (Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke opt-in, and Auto Label plus Check PR Size on the second run). 2 failure: `Check Changeset`, twice, judged in ③. ### ① Derived judgments

- **Which writes now open the door's unit — RIGHT.** `opensAfterAbortUnit` keeps its first line (an open ambient or threaded unit: no unit of its own; the closed-handle reading from PR #22894 kept), its `skipAutomations` exit, and its tail (the object's driver is the default one and declares transactions).
